My SO and I are adopting a puppy in 2 weeks. The Puppy is part Husky part Swiss Shepard, We already met the puppies and the owners, they are lovely people with a well raised dog (the mother). We've been watching all Cesar Milan's videos but I want to ask for any tips/ reading materials that would be useful.

 

More details:

 

  • We do not live together, but are always together.

 

  • My SO is deadly allergic to horses and cats, (we went over to the dog owner's place there where 2 big dogs and 5 puppies, we spent the evening he should no signs of allergies)

 

  • I used to have big dogs (10 years ago), a rott and a bullmastif, but I wasn't the one Training them.

Few things.

First off, Let a puppy be a puppy. Take time to let it explore this whole new world for him/her and to bond with it. Don't focus on one particular training technique before the puppy is actually there. All dogs are different and respond to different stimuli. For example i also watched all Cesar Milan videos and tried some of his techniques on my dog. It did not work. I tried a clicker and positive feedback technique and that worked a lot better for us. Easiest way to figure out what is best for you and the pup is to play. Lots of playing will help you see what stimuli he or she will react to best.

One of the most important things i've realized about raising a dog is being consistent. Both you and your SO need to set ground rules and stick with them. You don't want the dog on your sofa? Well make sure that you never allow it. Dogs do better when they have consistent owners.

Last thing, let a puppy be a puppy. Let him or her play, enjoy herself. Sure it will be able to sit on command in the first few days and come when called. But keep it at that. Dont start overtraining your new pup just because you think it's super smart. Let her grow up a bit and enjoy itself. There is plenty of time to train it when its old enough to go to school.
thank you, I do worry about the Training part, but I want the puppy to be happy.

Dont worry about it, it's a blast!

A puppy that you care for will try to please you and will enjoy when that happens.

But when training, start small. Keep a pocket full of small, 1 bite, treats and call its name. Everytime it reacts, give it a treat. Now stand 3 feet away and repeat. Increase the distance over time and the dog will realize that the words "Name" and "Here" means my human wants something from me, i should pay attention.

Then when you add more "tricks" like sit or down, its so much fun seeing them figuring out what you mean. Everytime my puppy even hinted at sitting down, i would say sit and praise her when she actually sat down. Over time that clicked with her and she understood what i meant.

But like i said. Playing with the dog is now really important and very fun.

Getting your puppy proper socialization will be key to having a well-adjusted and confident adult, but also don't go anywhere where he could encounter unvaccinated dogs until your puppy is fully vaccinated (so no Petsmart, Petco, etc). A puppy class with a good trainer is a really good environment to start with, since all the puppies will be at the same level of vaccinations and they usually do a lot of confidence-building exercises and little training tips. The Petsmart or Petco classes are not a good option; if you want help on finding one and don't know what to look for, you can PM me your location and I can give you some recommendations based on your area (not all trainers are created equal!).

For puppies, everything should be a super positive experience and they should be set up for success as much as possible. I wouldn't really take a lot of training advice from Cesar Milan, but he is on point about giving the dog plenty of exercise and not anthropomorphizing them. That being said, also don't do forced exercise with your puppy. If you have a backyard, let the puppy run about and play as much as he wants, but don't take him on long walks on hard surfaces or jogs or anything strenuous/forced until he gets older.

Lots of chew toys if you don't want your shoes to become chews! Puppy Kongs are great for little baby teeth, as they're softer and pretty hard to destroy. As your dog gets older, he'll need something tougher; I like black Kongs and toys from West Paw Design. If he bites you or nibbles, redirect him onto a toy. That's part of normal puppy behavior, but he has to gently learn that humans are not chew toys

Since you and your SO will always be together, make sure you are unified in what you are teaching the puppy. If you don't want the puppy to be on the couch, don't let your SO pick him up and put him on the couch when you're not around. If you want the puppy to look at you before receiving a treat, make sure that your SO also has the puppy look at him before receiving a treat. Consistency is super important for a puppy!

Otherwise, I highly recommend "Perfect Puppy in 7 Days" by Dr. Sophia Yin and "The Puppy Primer" by Dr. Patricia McConnell. Both are very respected animal behaviorists and that will give you a good start on raising a well-behaved and balanced dog.
